title: Placement survives a counter update
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $it,kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $s$ be a natural number. Suppose a memory map $\mu'$ places each item $j<A.n$ at address $A.dst+p_j$, where $p_j$ is the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)<kf(j)$ plus the number of indices $i<j$ with $kf(i)=kf(j)$. For every $t\le A.nb$, every integer $x$, and every $j<A.n$, changing the memory value at address $A.cnt+t$ to $x$ leaves the value at address $A.dst+p_j$ equal to $it(j)$.
hypotheses_covered: $A,it,kf$ satisfy the counting-sort preconditions for some resource limits and memory map
$\mu'$ has the shifted-state invariant at stage $s$
replaced:
Let a count-sort instance have $n$ items, source and destination starting addresses
$\mathrm{src}$ and $\mathrm{dst}$, key-cell address parameters
$\mathrm{key},\mathrm{stride},\mathrm{off}$, key bound $N_b$, and counter starting
address $\mathrm{cnt}$. Let memory be a function from natural-number addresses to
integers, and let $\mathrm{it}(i)$ and $\mathrm{kf}(i)$ denote the item and its key at
index $i$. Assume the word size bounds the memory-space size, all source, destination,
and counter ranges fit in memory, the source cells contain the items, and for every
$i<n$ the address $\mathrm{key}+\mathrm{it}(i)\,\mathrm{stride}+\mathrm{off}$ lies in
memory and contains key $\mathrm{kf}(i)<N_b$. Assume the source, destination, and
counter ranges are pairwise disjoint, and every item key-cell address lies outside both
the destination and counter ranges. Suppose a memory $\mu'$ places each item $j<n$ at
destination address $\mathrm{dst}+p_j$, where $p_j$ is the number of indices $i<n$ with
$\mathrm{kf}(i)<\mathrm{kf}(j)$ plus the number of indices $i<j$ with
$\mathrm{kf}(i)=\mathrm{kf}(j)$; also suppose that for every $u\le N_b$ with $s<u$,
counter cell $\mathrm{cnt}+u$ contains the number of indices $i<n$ with
$\mathrm{kf}(i)<u$, and for every $u<s$, counter cell $\mathrm{cnt}+u$ contains the
number of indices $i<n$ with $\mathrm{kf}(i)<u+1$. Then, for every $t\le N_b$, every
integer $x$, and every $j<n$, changing memory cell $\mathrm{cnt}+t$ to $x$ leaves item
$j$ at address $\mathrm{dst}+p_j$.
